title: Rosalind and the Asset
premise: Financial-crimes investigator Ines Vasquez has spent two years laundering her guilt through routine casework since the safe house raid that killed her witness and nearly killed her. When a real-estate listing surfaces with interior photos of that same safe house — including the hidden room where she once hid — she realizes someone inside the protection program is selling its secrets. Her investigation collides with Rosalind Achebe, the asset she failed to protect, now living under a new name and unwilling to be dragged back in. Together they trace the leak to Deputy Director Marcus Hale, who plans to eliminate Rosalind before she can testify at an international anti-corruption summit, staging her death as a gas explosion. Ines must choose between burning her career and the man who mentored her, or letting history repeat itself; they expose Hale publicly at the summit's eve, but Rosalind walks away from Ines, and survival costs them both the life they might have had.
about_author: Gideon Vasquez is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about the quiet violence of paperwork and the people it buries.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Insomniac Ines scrolls listings at 3 a.m. and finds her old safe house for sale, photos revealing the hidden closet where she crouched during the raid. She reports it internally and is told to stand down. Emotional beat: dread reawakened; the past is not past.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Assigned a mundane embezzlement case, she notices transaction patterns matching the listing agent's brokerage — shell layers too elegant for real estate. Her supervisor, Deputy Director Hale, gently redirects her. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Rosalind, Otherwise
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Living as 'Marion Cole' in Lisbon, Rosalind recognizes the safe house photos online and knows what it means: someone is hunting the program's ghosts. She begins erasing herself again. Emotional beat: exhausted vigilance; freedom was always rented.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Against orders, Ines flies to Lisbon using the case file's loose thread and finds Rosalind — alive, furious, armed. Rosalind gives her one hour to prove she isn't the leak. Emotional beat: hostility crackling with unfinished grief and old trust.

chapters.title: What the Raid Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Over one long night, each recounts the raid from her side: Ines the survivor's guilt, Rosalind the betrayal of being left behind. They compare timelines and realize only three people knew the safe house layout. Emotional beat: wounds opened become evidence.

chapters.title: The Brokerage
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind works her criminal contacts to trace the listing's photographer while Ines pulls financial records; the money routes back through a foundation tied to the summit's host committee. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership becoming genuine alliance.

chapters.title: Hale's House
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Confronting her mentor privately, Ines presents the trail; Hale admits knowledge but frames it as containment, warning that exposing him destroys the program and everyone in it. He offers her a promotion and silence. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity; power dressed as protection.

chapters.title: Scheduled Accident
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind discovers the plan: a gas-line 'failure' at her building timed for the summit's opening night, with her death closing the last testimony gap. She must decide whether to run forever or stand still and fight. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ines goes over Hale's head to the summit's oversight counsel while Rosalind lets herself be found, feeding Hale false confirmation of her location. The trap inverts: inspectors arrive at the rigged building as Hale arrives at the decoy. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; love expressed as coordinated risk.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Hale is arrested on the summit's first morning; Ines testifies, ending her career inside the agency she saved. Rosalind, free at last, chooses disappearance over reunion — leaving Ines a single photograph of the safe house door, finally closed. Emotional beat: costly victory; survival without restoration.
